newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Deng helped mould Hong Kong future law.
newsitem.headline: China's Deng helped mould Hong Kong future law.

text.p: China said on Sunday that its late leader Deng Xiaoping had personally given instructions to drafters of the constitution for Hong Kong after the British colony returns to Chinese rule.
During the four years and eight months of drafting work on the Basic Law, Deng constantly met members of the drafting committee to give instructions, the official Xinhua news agency said.

"Without his instructions and encouragement, it would have been impossible for us to complete the draft of this law which has both historical and international significance, in such a smooth way," it quoted Lu Ping, head of the Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office of the State Council, or cabinet, as saying.
The statement was made in one of the many tributes to Deng by China's official media since the death of the elder statesman on Wednesday at the age of 92.
China regains sovereignty over the British colony at midnight on June 30.
Beijing has maintained that the Basic Law -- drafted by people it selected from China and Hong Kong -- conformed with its promise that "Hong Kong people would rule Hong Kong".
It maintains that the territory's laws must comply with the Basic Law and final interpretation rests with China's parliament, the National People's Congress.
China's parliament is largely a rubber stamp body, designed to give a legal framework for decisions by the Communist Party's powerful Politburo.
China has already decided to scrap parts of some existing Hong Kong laws related to civil liberties, saying they did not conform with the Basic Law.
In a highly controversial move, it also plans to abolish the existing, elected legislature and replace it with an appointed provisional body.
